description: Tennessee-only rules checked against Tennessee Code Annotated section 55-8-152 in the General Assembly's 2024 code compilation, and against the Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual for the point system and graduated-license steps. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. A 2025 bill to raise the 70 mph controlled-access maximum was withdrawn and is not used.

questions.q: Except as provided for certain controlled-access highways, Tennessee Code makes it unlawful to drive on a highway or public road of the state in excess of
questions.explanation: Section 55-8-152(a) says that, except as provided in subsection (c), it is unlawful to operate or drive a motor vehicle on any highway or public road of this state in excess of 65 mph. The manual's separate statement that primary and secondary highways are 55 mph unless posted is not used as this statutory maximum.

questions.q: On a Tennessee controlled-access highway with four or more lanes that is on the state highway system or the interstate system, section 55-8-152 sets the maximum at
questions.explanation: Section 55-8-152(c) makes it unlawful to drive a motor vehicle or a truck in excess of 70 mph on all controlled-access highways with four or more lanes designated as being on the state system of highways or the state system of interstate highways. House Bill 1055 of 2025, which would have raised that figure to 75 mph, was withdrawn and is not the law used here.

questions.q: In the left-hand lane of those same Tennessee controlled-access highways, section 55-8-152 makes it unlawful to drive slower than
questions.explanation: Section 55-8-152(c) says that in the left-hand lane of those controlled-access highways it is unlawful to operate or drive a motor vehicle at a rate of speed less than 55 mph. The compilation does not state a 45 mph minimum for the right lane, so that manual figure is not used.

questions.q: A special school speed limit that a Tennessee county or municipality adopts beside school grounds
options: May be set below 15 mph whenever a flasher is installed
At least 15 mph, only with signs, a flashing light, and children present
Is 25 mph at all hours with no sign required
Is 20 mph within 300 feet of the school whether or not children are present
questions.explanation: Section 55-8-152(d)(1)(A) authorizes counties and municipalities to set a special speed limit, based on an engineering investigation, on a road adjacent to school grounds devoted primarily to normal school-day activity. That limit shall not be less than 15 mph, and it is in effect only when proper signs are posted with a warning flasher or flashers in operation and only while children are actually present. The exception for school entrances and exits to and from controlled-access highways on the state highway system is stated in the same subdivision.

questions.q: The Tennessee manual says it is unlawful to drive or be in physical control of a vehicle while the alcohol concentration of the operator's blood or breath is
options: .02 percent or higher for every driver
questions.explanation: The manual says it is unlawful to drive or be in physical control of a vehicle on a public street, highway, road, alley, or listed public premises while under the influence, or while the alcohol concentration of the operator's blood or breath is .08 percent or higher. It also says a driver can be convicted of DUI with a .00 reading if impaired by a drug.

questions.q: An adult Tennessee driver, age 18 or older, receives a notice of proposed suspension after accumulating
questions.explanation: The manual says adult drivers 18 or older who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension. An advisory letter is mailed to a licensee with 6 to 11 points in any 12 months.

questions.q: A Tennessee driver under 18 receives a notice of proposed suspension after accumulating
options: 6 or more points within a 12-month period
questions.explanation: The manual says juvenile drivers less than 18 who accumulate 6 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension. An advisory letter goes to a juvenile licensee with 1 to 5 points in any 12 months.

questions.q: A Tennessee learner permit requires the applicant to be 15, and the permit must be held 180 days before an intermediate restricted license. With the permit, the driver may not drive
questions.explanation: The manual says a learner-permit holder must be 15, pass the written exams and vision screening, and hold the permit 180 days. The holder may drive only when accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older in the front seat, and may not drive between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

questions.q: Before a Tennessee intermediate restricted license, a parent, legal guardian, or driving instructor must verify practice driving of
questions.explanation: The manual says the intermediate restricted applicant must be 16, pass the driving-skills test, have held a learner permit for 180 days, and have certification on form SF-1256 of fifty hours of driving experience, ten hours at night, signed by a parent, legal guardian, or licensed driving instructor.

questions.q: A Tennessee intermediate license holder may have only one other passenger unless
options: A passenger 21+ holds an unrestricted license
The driver has held the license for 30 days
questions.explanation: The manual says an intermediate licensee can have only one other passenger unless one or more passengers is 21 or older with a valid unrestricted license, or the passengers are brothers, sisters, step-siblings, or adopted or foster children living in the same house and the driver has a parent's letter authorizing them only for going to and from school.

questions.q: To move from a Tennessee intermediate restricted license to an intermediate unrestricted license, the driver must be 17 and have held the restricted license for
options: One year, with a qualifying record
Six months with any driving record
questions.explanation: The manual says the driver must be 17 and have held the intermediate restricted license for one year. The driver cannot have accumulated more than 6 points, or else must hold the restricted license an additional 90 days, cannot have had an at-fault traffic crash, and cannot have two safety-belt violations. A regular Class D license is available at 18, or earlier upon high-school graduation or a GED.

questions.q: A Tennessee driver may use a defensive driving course to avoid suspension, or to reduce a suspension period,
options: As many times as the driver is cited
questions.explanation: The manual says drivers may attend a defensive driving course to avoid license suspension or to reduce the suspension period, and that option is available only once in any five-year period.

questions.q: In Tennessee, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Tennessee issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Tennessee complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Tennessee requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Tennessee teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Tennessee requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In Tennessee, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Tennessee, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: In Tennessee, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Tennessee drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Tennessee car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Tennessee car knowledge test has 30 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Tennessee car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Tennessee car knowledge test.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Tennessee?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Tennessee can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Tennessee's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Tennessee: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Tennessee?
questions.explanation: Tennessee requires a car seat or booster until 9 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Tennessee's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Tennessee requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

provenance.manual: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security

questions.q: Under Tennessee's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Tennessee can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
